composition.story: Gas-bearing magma collects in the Magma reservoir beneath a blocked Conduit. Advance to see pressure open the Conduit. At the Vent, falling pressure lets gas expand and drive magma out as lava. This simplified example shows a gas-driven eruption.

aha.observation: As magma rises, falling pressure lets gas expand, helping drive magma through the Vent as lava.

states.label: Pressure builds
states.why: Magma and gas accumulate beneath a blocked Conduit, increasing pressure against the surrounding rock.

states.label: A path opens

states.label: Eruption
states.why: Lower pressure lets gas bubbles expand, helping push magma out; magma at the surface is called lava.
